slot.brief: Circuit of a cell with a resistor across which a voltmeter of given resistance is connected; find the voltmeter reading and the error caused by its finite resistance.

stem: An ideal $24$ V cell is connected to a $4\ \Omega$ resistor in series with an $8\ \Omega$ resistor. A $24\ \Omega$ voltmeter is connected across the $8\ \Omega$ resistor, as shown in the figure. What are its reading and the absolute error relative to the voltage without the voltmeter?

verdicts.working: With the voltmeter, the parallel resistance is 8||24 = 6 Ω, so the voltage across it is 24×6/(4+6) = 14.4 V. Without the voltmeter, the 8 Ω resistor has 24×8/(4+8) = 16 V across it; absolute error = 1.6 V.

working:
$R_{\parallel}=\dfrac{8\times24}{8+24}=6\ \Omega$; $V_{\mathrm{meter}}=24\dfrac{6}{4+6}=14.4\ \text{V}$
$V_0=24\dfrac{8}{4+8}=16\ \text{V}$
$\text{absolute error}=|16-14.4|=1.6\ \text{V}$

Independent check: With the voltmeter, the parallel resistance is 8||24 = 6 Ω, so the voltage across it is 24×6/(4+6) = 14.4 V. Without the voltmeter, the 8 Ω resistor has 24×8/(4+8) = 16 V across it; absolute error = 1.6 V.

figure.description: Draw a rectangular circuit loop. On the left vertical branch, draw an ideal cell labeled 24 V, with its positive terminal toward the top. On the top horizontal branch, place a resistor labeled 4 Ω, followed by a resistor labeled 8 Ω. Connect a voltmeter labeled 24 Ω in a separate branch directly across the 8 Ω resistor. Use standard circuit symbols and show no other components.

draft.distractor_notes: B: ignores the voltmeter’s loading. C: incorrectly treats the voltmeter as short-circuiting the resistor. D: reports the voltage across the series resistor as the error.
